newsitem.title: POLAND: Poison gas from oil well menaces Polish town.
newsitem.headline: Poison gas from oil well menaces Polish town.

text.p: Poisonous hydrogen sulphide gas leaking from an oil and natural gas drill shaft threatened the town of Debno in western Poland on Thursday and civil defence authorities urgently told residents to climb to upper floors of buildings.
"The situation at the moment is that there is an emergency," the area's civil defence inspector Stanislaw Smerwinski said on private Radio Zet.
"People should stay at home. If they smell hydrogen sulphide, as they do in Debno, they should go to higher buildings, to the second or third floor or higher," Smerwinski added.

PAP news agency quoted fire officials as saying the gas cloud stemmed from an explosion in the morning at an exploratory shaft near the village of Rozansk which led to concentrations of 10 percent of the deadly gas in the air for 300 metres around the site.
It said there was no information yet on any possible casualties.
All fire officers in the entire Gorzow province have been mobilised and police were halting all traffic into the area.
A special crisis committee convened in the provincial capital Gorzow and was considering the possiblity of evacuating Rozansk.
